Metastatic disease from bladder urothelial carcinoma

s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of a painless swelling over a pacemaker site with persistent systemic symptoms
salient_findings: Painless swelling over the pacemaker site
Persistent fatigue, dyspnea, and cough after COVID-19 infection
Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device on chest ultrasound
CT imaging confirmed a soft-tissue mass around the pacemaker pocket
key_facts: 70-year-old man with a history of nicotine use
Remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
Remote history of bladder urothelial carcinoma
Dual-chamber pacemaker implantation for sick sinus syndrome 9 months prior
Postoperative checks showed normal pacemaker function and a clinically unremarkable pocket
Tested positive for COVID-19 infection three weeks before presentation
Fatigue, dyspnea, and cough persisted and worsened after COVID-19 infection
New swelling over the pacemaker site reported at a routine cardiology visit
Normal blood pressure and heart rate on examination
No signs of cardiac decompensation or cachexia
Chest ultrasound revealed a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device
CT imaging excluded haematoma or infection

shortlist.label: Metastatic disease from laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma and new swelling at pacemaker site

shortlist.why_kept: Soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the device

shortlist.label: Lymphoma

raw.rationale: The presence of a soft tissue mass with increased vascularity surrounding the pacemaker device, as shown by chest ultrasound and CT imaging, along with the exclusion of haematoma or infection, supports the diagnosis of a sarcoma in the pacemaker pocket, particularly given the history of pacemaker implantation.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease from laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma
rejected.why: The remote history of laryngeal squamous cell carcinoma (7 years prior) makes it less likely to be the cause of the current symptoms, especially with no recent evidence of recurrence.

rejected.label: Metastatic disease from bladder urothelial carcinoma
rejected.why: Similar to the laryngeal cancer, the bladder urothelial carcinoma is 10 years in the past, making it an unlikely cause for the current presentation without other signs of metastasis.

rejected.label: Angiosarcoma
rejected.why: While angiosarcoma could present as a soft tissue mass, the specific location around the pacemaker and the patient's history of device implantation make pacemaker pocket sarcoma a more direct explanation.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: There's no specific indication of lymphoma in the provided key facts, such as lymphadenopathy or systemic symptoms suggestive of lymphoma, making it less likely than a localized process like pacemaker pocket sarcoma.
